_comment: Shared golden test vectors for cross-engine consistency (P3-6). Both tests/python/test_cipher_engine.py and tests/js/cipherEngine.test.mjs load this file and assert against it. See TO_FIX.md P3-6 and SHARED_CIPHER_VECTORS.md for full rationale.

cases.name: single_word_in_corpus
cases._note: Single-occurrence word, no case flag. Tango 3 + salt 47 = masked key 50.

cases.name: word_with_space_and_punctuation
cases._note: Two words separated by a space. Space = ~20 (U+0020 as hex).

cases.name: capitalized_word
cases._note: First letter capitalised -> ^C flag appended to coordinate.

cases.name: word_in_second_verso
cases._note: Single-occurrence word in second verso. Tests non-ascii char in corpus.

cases.name: punctuation_preserved
cases._note: Comma = ~2c (U+002C). Punctuation tokens interleave with word tokens.

cases.name: out_of_corpus_word
cases._note: Word absent from corpus -> PBKDF2-derived #hex fallback. Keystream is context-bound so ciphertext is not deterministic across runs, but decrypt(encrypt(x)) must round-trip to x in both engines.

cases.name: digit_run
cases._note: Consecutive digits are grouped as a single fallback token. Non-deterministic ciphertext; round-trip only.

cases.name: mixed_corpus_and_fallback
cases._note: 'el' is in corpus (deterministic), 'x' is not (fallback, non-deterministic). Round-trip only because the fallback token is context-bound.

cases.name: invalid_tango_id_raises
cases._note: Tango ID 99 does not exist in the corpus. Both engines must raise.

cases.name: metadata_key_raises
cases._note: Keys starting with '_' are metadata, not tangos. Both engines must reject them.
